lines: A master clock and metronome, giving a start pulse, twelve pulses to the beat and an audible click
Sets the tempo in beats per minute, 0 to 301
A voltage here takes over from the BPM knob, 0V to 10V across 0 to 300 beats per minute
Starts and stops the clock; the lamp in it is lit while the clock runs
A rise here starts or stops the clock
Sets the clock back to the first beat of the bar without stopping it; the lamp in it flashes on the first beat of every four
The lamp that flashes on every beat; pressing it does nothing
An audible click, a loud one on the first beat of each bar and a quieter one on the other three
A 10V pulse when the clock starts and on every reset
A 10V pulse twelve times a beat
A divider for METRO's stream of twelve pulses a beat: it passes the stream and the start pulse on, and gives one pulse out of every so many
Sets how many incoming pulses are counted between output pulses, 1 to 48; with twelve pulses to the beat, 3 gives a quarter of a beat and 12 a whole one
A voltage here takes over from the DIV. knob, 0V to 10V across 1 to 48 pulses
The start and reset pulses from METRO; a rise here also sets the count so that the next pulse counted is the first of a division
The stream of twelve pulses a beat that is counted
The lamp that flashes each time a division completes; pressing it does nothing
A 10V pulse each time the number of pulses set by DIV. has been counted
Copies the voltage arriving at the start and reset input
Copies the stream of pulses arriving at the twelve-pulse input
A sixteen-step trigger sequencer whose steps can be switched by hand or by a trigger of their own
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, about 15 to about 3840 beats per minute
The voltage here is added to the CLOCK knob, a volt doubling the tempo
Starts and stops the sequencer
With a cable here a rise steps the sequencer on and the internal clock is not used
Sets the sequencer back to the first step
A rise here sets the sequencer back to the first step
Sets how many of the sixteen steps are played before the pattern repeats, 1 to 16
The voltage here is added to the STEPS knob, a volt for each step
Switches on the step the sequencer is playing, so a pattern can be tapped in while it runs
A voltage above 0V here switches on the step the sequencer is playing
Switches off the step the sequencer is playing
A voltage above 0V here switches off the step the sequencer is playing
A 1ms 10V pulse on each step that is switched on
Switches its step on or off; the button is lit while that step is on
A rise here switches that step on or off
A trigger sequencer on a grid five across and sixteen down: each row of five squares is one step, and each of the five columns has its own trigger output
Freezes the grid for editing; with it off the pattern scrolls through the grid as the sequence runs
A rise here sets the sequence back to the first step
A rise here moves the sequence on by one step, firing the output of every lit square in that step
Switches its square on or off; a lit square fires its column's output when the sequence reaches its step
A 10V pulse lasting fifty samples when the sequence reaches a step with this column's square lit
A trigger sequencer on a grid five across and sixteen down: each row of five squares is one step, and each of the five columns has its own trigger output
Freezes the grid for editing; with it off the pattern scrolls through the grid as the sequence runs
A rise here sets the sequence back to the first step
A rise here moves the sequence on by one step, firing the output of every lit square in that step
Switches its square on or off; a lit square fires its column's output when the sequence reaches its step
A 10V pulse lasting fifty samples when the sequence reaches a step with this column's square lit
A sixteen-step control voltage sequencer with a slider for each step
Sets the voltage the sequence puts out on its step, 0V to 10V
Takes 5V off the output, so the sliders run -5V to +5V rather than 0V to 10V; the lamp is lit while it is on
A rise here sets the sequence back to the first step
A rise here moves the sequence on by one step
With a cable here the voltage chooses the step directly and the step and reset inputs are not used, 0V to 10V across the sixteen sliders
The voltage of the step the sequence is on
A sample player: it reads a .wav file from disk and plays it on a gate or a trigger, with control over the start point and the speed
The sample plays while the voltage here is above 0V, starting from the point set by START; with a cable in TRIG this jack is not used
A rise here plays the sample once from the point set by START
Sets the point in the sample that playing starts from, 0 for the beginning and 10 for the end
Moves the start point away from the setting of the START knob, by as much as the trimmer beside it allows
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, setting how far the voltage at the start input moves the start point
Shifts the playing rate, -5 to +5; at the centre the sample plays at its own rate, and far enough down it plays backwards
Changes the playing rate, by as much as the trimmer beside it allows
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, setting how far the voltage at the speed input changes the playing rate
Doubles the playing rate for every volt here
Plays the sample round and round without stopping, so that it can be used as an oscillator; a rise at TRIG restarts it from the beginning
Loads the previous .wav file in the same folder
A rise here loads the previous .wav file in the same folder
Loads the next .wav file in the same folder
A rise here loads the next .wav file in the same folder
The left channel of the sample, or the only channel of a mono file, full scale coming out as 5V
The right channel of the sample, or the only channel of a mono file, full scale coming out as 5V
Menu — Load Sample opens a file browser for choosing the .wav file to play
A small sample player: it reads a .wav file from disk and plays it once on a trigger
A rise here plays the sample once from the beginning
Loads the previous .wav file in the same folder
Loads the next .wav file in the same folder
Shifts the playing rate, -5 to +5; at the centre the sample plays at its own rate, and far enough down it plays backwards
The sample, full scale coming out as 5V; a stereo file is played from its left channel alone
Menu — Load Sample opens a file browser for choosing the .wav file to play
One mono channel of a modular mixer: it adds its signal to a stereo bus that runs through a row of these
Joins the channel to a solo group; 10V arriving here silences the channel unless its own SOLO is on
10V while this channel is soloed, to be carried on to the next channel of the solo group; link the last one back to the first
The left side of the stereo bus arriving from the channel before this one
The left side of the bus with this channel's share added
The right side of the stereo bus arriving from the channel before this one
The right side of the bus with this channel's share added
Turns down one side of the channel, the left side at one end of its travel and the right side at the other
A voltage here takes over from the PAN knob, 0V fully left, 5V centred and 10V fully right
Silences every other channel of the solo group; its lamp blinks while it is on
A rise here turns the solo on or off
Turns the channel on and off; its lamp is lit while the channel is on
A rise here turns the channel on or off
Multiplies the incoming signal by 0 to 2, leaving it unchanged at the centre
A voltage here takes over from the GAIN knob, 0V to 10V across a multiplier of 0 to 2
The signal this channel adds to the bus
A copy of this channel's signal after gain, on and solo, for feeding an effect
Note — the column of lamps beside the gain control is a meter, one lamp for each volt to 10V, and the topmost one stays lit for a moment once the signal passes 10V
One stereo channel of a modular mixer: it adds its two signals to a stereo bus that runs through a row of these
Joins the channel to a solo group; 10V arriving here silences the channel unless its own SOLO is on
10V while this channel is soloed, to be carried on to the next channel of the solo group; link the last one back to the first
The left side of the stereo bus arriving from the channel before this one
The left side of the bus with this channel's share added
The right side of the stereo bus arriving from the channel before this one
The right side of the bus with this channel's share added
Turns down one side of the channel, the left side at one end of its travel and the right side at the other
A voltage here takes over from the PAN knob, 0V fully left, 5V centred and 10V fully right
Silences every other channel of the solo group; its lamp blinks while it is on
A rise here turns the solo on or off
Turns the channel on and off; its lamp is lit while the channel is on
A rise here turns the channel on or off
Multiplies the incoming signals by 0 to 2, leaving them unchanged at the centre
A voltage here takes over from the GAIN knob, 0V to 10V across a multiplier of 0 to 2
The left signal this channel adds to the bus
The right signal this channel adds to the bus
A copy of this channel's left signal after gain, on, solo and pan, for feeding an effect
A copy of this channel's right signal after gain, on, solo and pan, for feeding an effect
Note — the column of lamps beside the gain control is a meter, one lamp for each volt to 10V, and the topmost one stays lit for a moment once the signal passes 10V
The end of a modular mixer's stereo bus: it takes the bus in, applies a level to it and sends it to the main outputs
The left side of the stereo bus arriving from the last channel
The right side of the stereo bus arriving from the last channel
Copies the left side of the bus as it arrives, before the gain and the on button, for carrying on elsewhere
Copies the right side of the bus as it arrives, before the gain and the on button, for carrying on elsewhere
Turns the main outputs on and off; its lamp is lit while they are on
Multiplies the bus by 0 to 2, leaving it unchanged at the centre
The left side of the bus after the gain and the on button
The right side of the bus after the gain and the on button
Note — the two columns of lamps are meters, one lamp for each volt to 10V, and the topmost one stays lit for a moment once that side passes 10V
Two sends for a modular mixer: each takes a signal, scales it and adds it to a send chain that passes through the module
The send chain arriving from another module; this half adds its own send to whatever is here
The chain signal of that half plus the signal at its IN, scaled by that half's SEND knob
Sets how much of that half's input signal is added to the chain, from none of it to all of it
A voltage here takes over from that half's SEND knob, 0V to 10V across none of the signal to all of it
The signal that half sends into the chain
Copies the signal at that half's IN, untouched
Ties the two halves together so that one SEND knob governs both; its lamp is lit while it is on
A sample and hold that doubles as a voltage source set by hand, with the value shown on a display
The voltage that is followed and held; while nothing has been held the module passes this voltage straight through
Captures the voltage at the input and holds it; the lamp is lit while a value is being held
A rise here captures the voltage at the input and holds it
Adds one to the held value, rounding a fractional value upwards to a whole number
Takes one off the held value, rounding a fractional value downwards to a whole number
The held value
Combines two voltages with one of six operations, chosen by the buttons; the chosen one is lit
The first of the two voltages combined; an empty jack counts as 0V
The second of the two voltages combined; an empty jack counts as 0V
Sets the operation to addition, a plus b
Sets the operation to subtraction, a minus b
Sets the operation to multiplication, a times b
Sets the operation to division, a divided by b; while b is at 0V the output holds the value it had
Sets the operation to the larger of the two voltages
Sets the operation to the smaller of the two voltages
The result of the chosen operation
Applies one of twenty-one mathematical functions to a voltage, naming the chosen one on the display
The voltage the function is applied to
Steps forward through the list of functions
Steps back through the list of functions
The result of the function applied to the input voltage
Note — the functions in order are abs, round, ceil, floor, pow2, sqrt, exp, log, log10, cos, sin, tan, acos, asin, atan, cosh, sinh, tanh, acosh, asinh and atanh
Note — the red lamps light when the chosen function has no finite answer for the voltage at the input, such as the square root of a negative one
Passes one of two signals and switches between them on a trigger, the way a closed hi-hat cuts an open one short
The signal passed while the trigger below it was the last of the two to fire
A rise here switches the output to the signal above this jack
Fades one of the two signals down, -1 to +1: at one end the first signal falls silent, at the other the second does, and at the centre both pass at full level
Whichever of the two signals is selected
Four signal lines, each with a solo and an on switch that can be pressed or triggered
The signal for that line
Silences the other three lines while it is on; its lamp blinks while it is on
A rise here turns that line's solo on or off
Turns that line on and off; its lamp is lit while the line is on
A rise here turns that line on or off
That line's signal, silent while the line is off or another line is soloed
A quantiser that rounds a voltage down to one of a number of even steps
Sets how many steps the range of 0V to 10V is cut into, 1 to 32; the number is shown on the display
An attenuverter, -10 to +10, setting how far the voltage at the steps input changes the number of steps
Changes the number of steps away from the knob setting, by as much as the trimmer allows
The voltage to be rounded
The input voltage rounded down to the nearest step
A limiter for a stereo pair, with a make-up gain after it
Multiplies the limited signal by 0 to 10; the lamp under it lights when the result passes 10V
Sets the voltage past which the signal is squeezed, 10V leaving it alone and 0V squeezing everything; the lamp under it lights while the limiter is working
One of the two signals to be limited
That side of the limited and made-up signal
A pair of rough filters for a stereo signal, one cutting the top of the band and one the bottom
Sets how many poles each filter has, 1 to 8; more poles give a steeper slope
Ties the two cut controls together so that they move as one, keeping the gap between them; its lamp is lit while it is on
Sets the frequency above which the signal is cut, with nothing cut at the top of its travel
A voltage here takes over from the high cut control, 0V to 10V across its travel
Sets the frequency below which the signal is cut, with nothing cut at the bottom of its travel
A voltage here takes over from the low cut control, 0V to 10V across its travel
One of the two signals to be filtered
That side of the filtered signal
A delay line of as many as 9999 samples, with a feedback input and a second mode that turns it into a crude filter
Switches to a mode in which the output is the feedback signal less the average of the buffer, which acts as a crude filter, and in which the buffer is a tenth as long; its lamp is lit while it is on
Scales the signal at the FB IN jack before it is written into the buffer, from none of it to all of it
Sets the length of the delay, 1 to 9999 samples
The signal written into the buffer
A second signal added into the buffer, scaled by the feedback knob
A voltage here takes over from the LENGTH knob, 0V to 10V across 1 to 9999 samples
The signal read back out of the buffer, clamped to -10V to +10V
A distortion that multiplies the signal up and folds back whatever passes 5V
Multiplies the signal by five times its setting, 0 to 10
Sets how much of what passes 5V is folded back: at 0 the signal is clipped flat at 5V, and higher settings fold it further back
The signal to be distorted
A voltage here takes over from the GAIN knob, 0V to 10V
A voltage here takes over from the FOLD knob, 0V to 10V
The distorted signal
A wireframe cube turning on two axes on its screen, with the depth of one of its corners as the output
Sets the rate of the turn on one of the two axes; with the jack empty that rate is 0.5
Sets the rate of the turn on the other axis; with the jack empty that rate is 0.5
The depth coordinate of one corner of the cube, multiplied by 5
A patch bay for taking cables out of the way: jacks are joined to each other by the lines drawn on the panel
Whatever arrives here comes out of the jack the panel line joins it to
Carries whatever arrives at the input the panel line joins it to
One of three inputs that are added together
The three inputs of the group added together
A panel one space wide carrying a line of text, for labelling part of a patch
Menu — Label opens a box for typing the text; the first twenty characters are shown
A blank panel showing the red eye of HAL 9000
